title: Add verify command timeout evidence
instructions:
Implement only Slice 3 of Core worker execution trust hardening: add timeout handling and evidence for evaluateWorkerResult verify commands. Do not add setup command timeout or worker runtime timeout in this slice.

Required behavior:
- Add an optional TaskSpec verifyTimeoutMs?: number field.
- Apply a bounded timeout to each harness-run verify command. Use a conservative default when verifyTimeoutMs is absent.
- When a verify command times out, terminate the process, return a VerifyCommandResult with non-zero exitCode, timedOut: true, timeoutMs, and timeoutDetails evidence, and make evaluation pass false.
- Preserve Slice 2 sequential behavior: after a timeout result, do not execute later verify commands.
- Preserve VerifyCommandResult stdout, stderr, command, timing fields, changed-file collection, scope checks, no-op writer pass gate behavior, report-only behavior, and worker verify evidence parsing.
- Do not add setup command timeout, worker runtime timeout, command-runner timeout, CLI surface, daemon/watch behavior, dashboard behavior, remote adapter behavior, multi-project orchestration, writerCap changes, hidden memory, LLM semantic verification, task templates, agent profile edits, run lifecycle changes, or documentation edits.

Required tests:
- A verify command that exceeds verifyTimeoutMs records timedOut true, timeoutMs, timeoutDetails, non-zero exitCode, and makes evaluation fail.
- A timed-out verify command stops later verify commands from running.
- Normal verify commands still pass with timedOut false or omitted false-compatible evidence and timing fields intact.
- Existing sequential verification, scope, no-op, report-only, and advisory worker verification tests still pass.

Implementation guidance: keep the timeout implementation local to worker-result verification. Prefer a small private default constant and helper rather than broad command runner changes. Use a short timeout in tests to keep the suite fast and deterministic. End with exactly one HARNESS_RESULT line.
